predecessors.name: Ceylon (Sinhalese kingdoms)
predecessors.text: the island's Sinhalese kingdoms, Cliopatria's Ceylon row to 1506

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Kotte
predecessors.text: Kotte, ceded to the Portuguese crown on 27 May 1597

successors.name: Dutch Ceylon
successors.text: the coast the Dutch took from the Portuguese between 1639 and June 1658: Batticaloa and Trincomalee (1639), Galle (1640), Colombo (1656), Jaffna (1658)

ledger.x: 1505: the Portuguese reach Ceylon and agree a trade treaty with the King of Kotte at Colombo.
1560: Viceroy Dom Constantino de Bragança's first expedition takes Mannar Island from Jaffna.
1565: Dharmapala of Kotte takes refuge at Colombo under Portuguese protection.
1582: Jaffna is paying tribute to the Portuguese.
1597 (bridging, page silent): Portuguese ports on the south and east coasts.
27 May 1597: Dharmapala dies and Kotte passes to the Portuguese crown.
1597: direct Portuguese rule begins in Ceylon with the cession of Kotte.
1612 (bridging, page silent): the Portuguese leave Kandy.
1619: the tributary kingdom of Jaffna is conquered.
1619: the Portuguese conquer the Jaffna kingdom.
1654: the Dutch and Portuguese fight for Colombo.
1656: the contest for Colombo ends with the Dutch capture (next event).

wars.name: Sinhalese–Portuguese War
wars.outcome: The Portuguese held the coast and lost it to the Dutch (allies of Kandy from 1638); Kandy kept the interior.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Jaffna kingdom
wars.outcome: Cankili II defeated by Filipe de Oliveira; the kingdom ended in 1619 and passed to Portuguese Ceylon.

wars.name: Dutch–Portuguese War
wars.outcome: The Dutch, first with Kandy, took Batticaloa (1639), Galle (1640), Colombo (1656) and Jaffna (June 1658); Portugal ceded Ceylon in 1661.

wars.name: Sitawaka attacks on Kotte
wars.outcome: Kotte lost most of its land to Sitawaka and its king took refuge at Colombo under Portuguese protection (1565); after Sitawaka fell in 1594 the lowlands were re-annexed to Kotte.

certainty.note: A trading post and a protected Kotte, with no boundary on any page; the Colombo disc and the Mannar Island disc are the smallest regions the grid draws.
No treaty or survey line is on the pages opened (the Luso–Kandyan Treaty of 1633 has no terms on S1); the inland frontier against Kandy was fluid (S4) and the corrected shape is a minimum.
